actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

device.name: Isaac Drone Racer (Isaac Lab Gymnasium environment)

facts.text: The drone racing task is registered as a standard Gym environment with the ID Isaac-Drone-Racer-v0
Isaac-Drone-Racer-v0 is registered with entry_point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv, the environment configuration DroneRacerEnvCfg and the env checker disabled
Isaac-Drone-Racer-Play-v0 is registered the same way with the configuration DroneRacerEnvCfg_PLAY
The project is an open-source simulation framework for autonomous drone racing built on IsaacLab
The Isaac Sim badge pins version 4.5.0
The setup instructions require the IsaacLab v2.1.0 release tag
The default scene spawns 4096 environments with env_spacing 0.0
The policy observation group concatenates the position, attitude, linear velocity, angular velocity, target position in the body frame and last action terms, with corruption disabled
The default configuration disables the critic observation group (observations.critic = None)
The environment uses decimation 4 and a simulation step of 1/400 s, so one environment step advances 0.01 s of simulated time
The episode length is 20 s (episode_length_s = 20)
The episode terminates on a time out, when the drone is more than 20 m from the target gate, and on an illegal contact above threshold 0.01
The track configuration places seven gates; gate 1 is at (0.0, 0.0, 1.0) and gate 4 at (-5.0, -5.0, 2.5)
The reset pose range is x from -3.5 to -1.5, y from -0.5 to 0.5 and z written as (1.5, 0.5), with all linear and angular velocities zero
The default action configuration disables the motor model (use_motor_model=False)
The action term stores four raw actions per environment
The raw action is clamped to [-1, 1] and mapped by (x + 1) / 2 to a motor speed up to omega_max
The action configuration declares arm length 0.035 m, thrust coefficient 2.25e-7 and omega_max 5145 rad/s, the last computed from a 1950 KV motor on a 6S battery at 4.2 V per cell
The processed action is applied as a body-z thrust and a three-axis body moment
The drone is a simulated USD articulation spawned from assets/5_in_drone/5_in_drone.usd, not a hardware connection

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the state this package's fake starts from; the upstream environment runs on Isaac Sim/PhysX and its determinism was not measured here, so no exact claim is made

gaps: the fake backend integrates only the total rotor thrust along the body z axis: the rigid-body flight dynamics, the body moments, aerodynamic drag, contacts and the USD drone asset of the upstream Isaac Sim scene are not modelled
the observation layout is inferred from the six concatenated policy terms of the environment configuration (20 values) and was not read from a running Isaac Sim environment
the fake action bounds of -1 to 1 per component mirror the clamp of the action term; the gym action space is created by isaaclab.envs.ManagerBasedRLEnv outside the clone and was not read
the 20 s time limit and the 20 m flyaway termination are modelled; the collision termination, the gate-passing command logic and the reward terms are not (the fake reward is always 0.0)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
the environment was never run: Isaac Sim 4.5.0, Isaac Lab v2.1.0 and a GPU are required, the fake was not compared with the upstream environment and nothing was validated against a physical device

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
